rubric.why: A complete definition identifies the subject matter of physics and the relationship it studies.
rubric.description: States that physics studies matter, energy, and their relationship.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for all three ideas; 1 mark if the definition is substantially correct but incomplete.

modelAnswer: Physics is the branch of science that deals with the study of matter, energy, and the relationship between them.

items.followUp: Define a vector and give two examples.

rubric.why: A scalar is distinguished from a vector by having magnitude but no direction.
rubric.description: Defines a scalar as a quantity with magnitude only and no direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining feature of a scalar.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate that the student can identify scalar quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

modelAnswer: A scalar is a physical quantity that has magnitude only and no direction.
Examples of scalars are mass and time.

rubric.why: Position describes where an object is in relation to a reference point.
rubric.description: Defines position as the location of an object relative to a reference point.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for both the object's location and its reference; 1 mark if only the idea of location is given.

modelAnswer: Position is the location of an object relative to a reference point.

items.followUp: How is natural gas formed from the remains of organisms?

rubric.why: Biogas is produced when microorganisms decompose biomass without oxygen.
rubric.description: Explains that bacteria decompose biomass in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential preparation process.

rubric.why: Methane is the main combustible component of biogas.
rubric.description: Identifies methane as the main useful gas in biogas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying methane as the main component or fuel.

modelAnswer: Biogas is prepared by allowing bacteria to decompose biomass in the absence of oxygen.
The process produces biogas, which contains methane as its main combustible component.

items.followUp: A 20 kg body is raised 5 m. Find its potential energy if g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Gravitational potential energy is calculated using mass, gravitational acceleration, and height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.description: Gives the correct potential energy with a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1500 J or its equivalent.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 50 kg, h = 3 m, g = 10 m s⁻²
Substitution: PE = 50 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 3 m

items.followUp: Define a moment of force and state its formula.

rubric.why: A rigid body is treated as not changing its shape or size under applied forces.
rubric.description: Defines a rigid body as one whose shape and size do not change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining property of a rigid body.

rubric.why: The axis of rotation is the line about which the body turns.
rubric.description: Defines the axis of rotation as the line around which a body rotates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the axis of rotation.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when forces act on it.
The axis of rotation is the imaginary straight line around which a body rotates.

items.followUp: Why is electrical energy useful in homes and industries?

rubric.why: The preferred form referred to is electrical energy.
rubric.description: Identifies electrical energy as the most preferred form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming electrical energy.

rubric.why: Electrical energy is convenient because it can be transmitted and changed into other forms.
rubric.description: Gives a valid reason for its preference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is easily converted into other forms or transmitted over long distances.

modelAnswer: Electrical energy is the most preferred form of energy.
It can be transmitted over long distances and easily converted into other forms of energy.

items.followUp: Define stress and strain, and write the formula for Young's modulus.

rubric.why: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of stress to strain within the elastic limit.
rubric.description: States the definition of Young's modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ratio definition and the elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain.
rubric.description: Writes a correct formula for Young's modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

modelAnswer: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain, within the elastic limit.
